extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news editors, media scholars, journalism students, and policy-makers interested in democratic news values
extracted.subtask_description: A set of evaluative criteria for selecting and judging news stories grounded in journalism's democratic/civic role — i.e., how journalism serves citizens as the Fourth Estate by informing, holding power to account, and preserving plurality and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interest / civic significance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize coverage that contributes to citizens' ability to participate in democratic life; emphasize civic relevance over mere audience appeal or entertainment value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Holding power (government, corporate, institutional) to account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus reporting on scrutiny of public and private institutions, exposing abuses, failures, or decisions with public consequence; treats watchdog function as central.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from interests
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain editorial autonomy from political actors and commercial pressures; avoid conflicts of interest that undermine credibility or skew coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of perspectives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure plurality in sources and perspectives so coverage reflects a multiplicity of publics and mitigates dominance by powerful voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information citizens need
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between what audiences desire (sensational, entertainment) and what they require to make informed civic decisions; privilege explanatory, contextual, and service journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative depth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue deeper inquiry, document-based reporting, and verification rather than relying solely on press releases or official accounts; aim to uncover hidden facts and systemic issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply critical scrutiny and analysis to claims and events rather than merely transcribing officials' words; interpret implications and challenge assertions where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to citizen needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Attunement and responsiveness to what citizens require from news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be receptive to the informational needs and concerns of communities, tailoring coverage to address practical civic questions and service-oriented information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical standards — Truth-telling
rubrics_metrics.description: Adherence to ethical norms, foremost truth-telling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uphold accuracy, fairness, and ethical conduct in newsgathering and reporting; weigh boldness against ethical caution to avoid causing unjust harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concern about concentrated ownership / plurality of voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch for concentrated media ownership and its impact on plurality of voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that ownership concentration can constrain diversity and investigative capacity; advocate institutional arrangements and editorial practices that preserve plurality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and management of tensions between values
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance competing journalistic values and pressures (e.g., independence vs commercial pressures; boldness vs ethical caution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly acknowledge trade-offs such as independence versus commercial viability, investigative ambition versus ownership constraints, and public service versus profit motives; make editorial choices transparently and consider institutional reforms to mitigate conflicts.
